text:
sarah_support: heads up — PayFlux (customer) opened an escalated ticket: for the last ~6h their EU users are seeing 600–900ms p50 and a bunch of 401/429 spikes. They say requests are being routed to our us-west POP. I ran a quick trace and pasted relevant bits below. Can net/sre triage?

sarah_support: repro snippets from customer (they sent):
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (34.216.10.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example.com
> Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized

# from a Frankfurt client: traceroute shows hop to us-west edge
traceroute to api.redwood.example.com (34.216.10.12), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1 ...
 7  54.240.2.1  180 ms
 8  34.216.10.12  190 ms
```

sarah_support: customer pasted DNS/dig results from their resolver and from 8.8.8.8:
```
# customer resolver (ISP):
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @their-resolver
34.216.10.12
$ dig +nocmd +noshort +additional api.redwood.example.com @their-resolver
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.example.com. 3600 IN A 34.216.10.12
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
... (TTL 3600)

# google public DNS:
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8
18.197.33.9
```

mike_oncall: thanks — can you add the raw edns-client-subnet and full dig +trace from the affected client? also paste last 5 auth request ids if you have them.

sarah_support: adding what customer provided:
```
$ dig +trace api.redwood.example.com @their-resolver
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +trace api.redwood.example.com @their-resolver
. . .
;; Received 512 bytes
api.redwood.example.com. 3600 IN A 34.216.10.12
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 54321
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 2
;; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 1232
;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:
;CLIENT-SUBNET: 0.0.0.0/0 (not present)  # ISP stripped ECS
```

ravi_net: looking — initial hypothesis: ISP resolver is returning a stale/warm cache IP that maps to us-west. Their resolver likely strips EDNS-Client-Subnet (ECS) and/or is returning a cached answer from an earlier propagation window. TTLs show 3600 which is high for geo failover entries. A couple notes:
- our authoritative returns different A records per region (geoip-based). If upstream resolver ignores EDNS or uses an old cached answer, they get us-west IP.
- some ISPs prefetch and hold entries beyond TTL under heavy load -> warm/cohort caching.

ravi_net: quick checks I ran from our vantage:
```
# from eu-checker (ams):
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @our-authoritative
18.197.33.9
# from us-west-checker:
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @our-authoritative
34.216.10.12
# authoritative: geo-db shows FR->EU mapping OK
# but we pushed a geo-db update 2h ago (sync to edge was in progress)
```

alexa_sre: adding symptom linking: when EU traffic lands in us-west we see increased token validation latency and occasional 401s because token issuer region affinity checks a region-scoped session store and KV/cache misses cause reauth. For some customer requests we also see duplicate retries -> doubled billing events.

kevin_csm: customer is upset about both UX and unexpected billing bump. They see >2x token refreshes and extra requests billed. They want a workaround today and a permanent fix.

mike_oncall: immediate mitigation options (short-term):
- lower authoritative TTL for geo A records to 60s (reduces caching lifetime) — can be rolled in a canary to avoid global churn.
- push urgent geo-db sync and confirm all edge caches got latest mapping.
- add region pinning fallback: when JWT indicates EU tenant, prefer EU auth endpoint (route via our control-plane override) until DNS steady.

ravi_net: agreed. action plan:
1) roll TTL down to 60s for geo A records in a 10% canary across authoritative nodes (ravi).
2) force geo-db resync to all edge POPs and verify checksums (ravi + dns_bot).
3) SRE to enable auth-region pinning for the PayFlux org for next 12h (alexa).
4) outreach to customer with repro steps and short-term mitigation (sarah + kevin).

alexa_sre: I'll also add a guard in the token validation path to accept a short grace window for sessions validated in another region to avoid immediate 401s during DNS flip. That should reduce billing duplicate retries.

kevin_csm: customer asked for ETA. Can we do steps 1+2 in the next 30m? they want to watch metrics.

ravi_net: starting TTL canary now. will post updates.

dns_bot: started geo-db resync to edges at 1715004600. job id: resync-2024-1715004600

ravi_net: resync completed on primary edges, still waiting on 3 regional caches to confirm checksum (checking).

mike_oncall: alexa — once pin is enabled, I'll monitor auth 5xx/401 and billing spike counts and report.

sarah_support: customer updated: they switched their app to 8.8.8.8 and report immediate improvement (latency down to 80–120ms). they want a permanent fix for users on their ISP.

ravi_net: final notes / root cause guess: authoritative mapping was correct but propagation + high TTL + ISP resolver cohort caching (plus ECS stripping) made some EU clients get an old us-west answer. The geo-db push during the window made it worse for clients hitting stale resolvers.

mike_oncall: postmortem action items (to do):
- reduce default geo A TTL to 300s and use aggressive canary for future geo-db pushes (ravi).
- implement ECS-aware fallback heuristics in routing logic so we prefer region by token/tenant metadata if ECS is missing (product/infra).
- add telemetry to detect resolver-cohort hotpaths and alert when >1% of requests from a region resolve to non-local POP for >10 minutes (sre).

kevin_csm: I'll send a summary and credits adjustment offer to PayFlux once we have the mitigation in place.

dns_bot: geo-db resync confirmations received from all edges at 1715004900. checksum: abc123def

ravi_net: all done for now, monitoring. please DM if you see fresh 401/429s from PayFlux org.

sarah_support: customer notified and will watch for 24h. closing loop here but leaving thread open for 24h monitoring. :thumbsup:
